unit_of_analysis: one section of a law textbook (owner decision)
what_this_is: Explicit quality criteria for the section-level multimodal corpus, each with the measurement that produced it and a threshold fixed in this record. C3 and C4 come from the executed text-only ablation, so visual need is measured rather than rated.

checks.name: C2 text-layer fidelity (median CER vs text layer)
checks.expected: <= 0.05 so the text layer, not OCR, is the reference

checks.name: C3 measured visual need (share of items unanswerable from text)
checks.expected: >= 0.30 for a corpus to support multimodal TQA

checks.name: C4 figure-attributable gain (share the figure made answerable)
C4b chunks with >=1 figure-attributable item
checks.expected: the usable multimodal subset of the frame

checks.name: C5 evidence-span tractability (median section chars)
checks.expected: <= 3000 so a verbatim-evidence gate stays discriminative

checks.name: C5b sections over 20k chars
checks.expected: 0; a 200k-char span makes any single quote trivially findable

checks.name: C7 rights eligibility
checks.expected: every frame unit clears rules 1 and 2

checks.name: C8 no reuse of sealed chunks
checks.value: FRESH under §7 as written: no audited unit shares source bytes or any 8-word pas
checks.expected: no shared source bytes and no shared passage

length_measure: Every character count in this record is raw len() on the section text exactly as the manifest carries it, because that is the string the gate searches. An NFC-normalised, whitespace-collapsed count of the same sections gives median 5925 and maximum 207673; both are correct measures of different things, and mixing them in one report was a defect in an earlier draft of this record.
the_binding_defect: C5. The section is the right unit for teaching content but its length is uncontrolled: median 7530 characters, maximum 265885, with 14 sections over 20k. A verbatim evidence gate over a span that long is nearly free to satisfy, so the gate stops discriminating between prompts. This is a property of the DATA as presented to the method, and it is what any method adaptation has to address.
